chunks: 394 - Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Shadhan al-Nishapuri said:

Five hundred dirhams, short of twenty dirhams, were deposited with me. I did not like for this amount to be short, so I weighed twenty dirhams from my own money and sent them to al-Asadi. I did not inform him of the shortage, nor that I had completed the amount from my own wealth. The reply came: 'The five hundred, of which twenty were yours, have reached us.' Al-Asadi died upon apparent justice (honesty), he did not change, and no one raised an objection against him in the month of Rabi' al-Akhar in the year 312 AH.

key_terms.ثَلَاثَمِائَةٍ: Three hundred (referring to the year 312 AH)
key_terms.رَبِيعَ الْآخِر: Rabi' al-Akhar (the fourth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the five hundred dirhams and the integrity of al-Asadi in Shia sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the reliability of the Four Deputies during the Minor Occultation, specifically illustrating the concept of *adalah* (integrity) through a subtle test of honesty. Muhammad ibn Shadhan’s decision to cover the missing twenty dirhams without informing al-Asadi served as a silent verification of the agent's trustworthiness, confirming that the Imam’s appointees were not only legally competent but also morally upright. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the infallible-like precision of the deputies' financial and administrative duties during the period of concealment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 394 - Muhammad Ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali Ibn Muhammad from Muhammad Ibn Shadhan Nishapuri that:

Five hundred dirhams short of twenty were deposited before me. I did not like it to be short of this amount, so I weighed another twenty dirhams from my money and sent the amount to Asadi. I did not inform him that I had completed it from my own money. The answer came: “The five hundred, of which twenty were yours, reached us.” Asadi died in the Rabiul Aakhir of the year three hundred and twelve. He was honest, he never changed, and he was not mentioned disrespectfully.
